config.title: Build CSV export endpoint with streaming

intro.title: Build CSV export endpoint with streaming
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Node.js API endpoint that exports data as a CSV file using streaming. You will learn how to use Node.js streams to efficiently generate and send large CSV files without consuming excessive memory. The core concept involves creating a readable stream for the CSV data and piping it directly to the HTTP response. You will work with the built-in `stream` module and the `csv-writer` library to structure the data. By the end, you will have a functional endpoint that streams CSV data to the client on demand.
intro.usecase: Streaming CSV export endpoints are essential for handling large datasets in production applications, such as financial reporting dashboards or e-commerce analytics platforms. For example, when a user clicks 'Export to CSV' on an admin panel displaying thousands of sales records, this pattern allows the server to send data incrementally, preventing memory overload and enabling immediate download initiation. Developers implement this to support features like real-time data exports from user-filtered tables or scheduled report generation in background jobs, ensuring efficient resource usage and a responsive user experience even with massive data volumes.

objectives: Construct a Node.js HTTP server endpoint that handles CSV export requests
Configure response headers to specify CSV content type and enable streaming
Initialize a writable stream to pipe data directly to the HTTP response
Manipulate data structures to format rows into CSV-compatible strings
Integrate a data source with the streaming pipeline to generate CSV content
Control the streaming flow to handle backpressure and memory efficiently
Implement error handling for both stream creation and data processing stages

steps.title: Configure response headers for CSV download
steps.instruction: Inside the server's request handler, set the response headers to indicate a CSV file download. Use res.setHeader() to set 'Content-Type' to 'text/csv' and 'Content-Disposition' to 'attachment; filename="data.csv"'.
steps.hint: The Content-Type header tells the browser the data format. The Content-Disposition header with 'attachment' prompts a file download with the specified filename.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to send proper headers for CSV file downloads when the endpoint is accessed.
successCriteria: The request handler includes res.setHeader() calls for 'Content-Type' and 'Content-Disposition' with correct values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've set some headers, but make sure both 'Content-Type' and 'Content-Disposition' are properly configured.
steps.feedbackWrong: The headers aren't set correctly. Check the syntax for res.setHeader() and the required values.
